newsitem.title: USA: Tropical depression forms off coast of Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Tropical depression forms off coast of Nicaragua.

text.p: A tropical depression formed off the northeast coast of Nicaragua on Monday and could strengthen into Tropical Storm Marco within a day or two, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 4 p.m. EST (2100 GMT), the center of the depression was located 145 miles (235 km) east-southeast of Cabo Gracias a Dios, a small city located near Nicaragua's border with Honduras, forecasters said.
The depression had maximum sustained winds of 35 mph (55 kph), and was expected to slowly strengthen overnight.

"We think it's going to meander around out in the Caribbean for a day or two, then start inching toward Jamaica," hurricane center forecaster Max Mayfield said. "There's a good chance of it making it into a tropical storm, but we don't think the environment is right for it to become a hurricane."

If its sustained winds top 39 mph (62 kph), the depression will become Tropical Storm Marco, the 13th in a series of named storms during this year's Atlantic hurricane season. A tropical storm graduates to hurricane status when its maximum winds exceed 74 mph (119 kph).
"This thing has been sitting down there for nearly a week, sputtering along and trying to develop, and it's finally gotten better organized," Mayfield said.
